# Columbia CKI: "Powering Data" (23 January 2026)

Authors: Hyae Ryung Kim, Ariela Farchi Behar, Isabel Hoyos, Una Oljaca, Shubhangi Prasad, Yosafat Partogi Simbolon, Clara Zibell, Gernot Wagner

## Key Findings (recovered via Exa PDF fetch)

### Executive Summary
- Data centers on track to **triple global electricity use by 2035**, with AI the dominant driver.
- By 2030, data centers could consume **~1,000 TWh/year, ~3% of world demand**.
- Despite surging demand, emissions can plateau if data centers increasingly powered by renewables.
- By 2030, **>50% of data center power projected to be renewable**, but fossil fuels (gas, coal in China/US) remain near-term source.
- **US and China alone account for 80% of growth** — epicenter of opportunity and grid stress.
- Europe grows slower but faces permitting and public pushback. India rapidly emerging as next hub.
- US grid faces long interconnection queues, increasing household bills, local moratoriums.
- Pushing developers to "power first" siting, behind-the-meter solutions: onsite renewables, SMRs, geothermal.
- China's state-led "Eastern Data, Western Computing" model enables speed and grid decompression.
- Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta control **>50% of capacity** and are biggest US renewable buyers.
- Efficiency gains (GPUs, custom chips, liquid cooling, model architectures like DeepSeek) can cut energy use by **10-40x**, but unlikely to fully offset demand growth.
- AI-driven grid optimization (VPPs, predictive load shifting), geothermal baseload could be game changers.

### Regional Projections (IEA base case, 2020-2030)
- US: +240 TWh by 2030 (+130%)
- China: +175 TWh by 2030 (+170%)
- Europe: +45 TWh by 2030 (+70%)
- Data centers expected to make up **30-40% of new energy demand** between 2024 and 2030.
- Emissions from data centers projected to plateau then decrease as supply decarbonizes.

### Data Center Clusters
- US, EU, UK, China host **9 of 10 largest data center clusters** globally by capacity (GW).
- >15% of global data center capacity under development concentrated in top 10 markets.
